checks.label: The page actually loads
checks.question: Will someone who clicks the ad reach the page at all?
checks.method: The navigation response is an HTTP 2xx, and the URL the browser ended on has the same hostname as the one requested (ignoring a leading "www.").
checks.detail: Responded HTTP 200 and stayed on neemans.com.

checks.label: Your tags are installed and firing
checks.question: Are Google Analytics and the Meta Pixel actually on this page?
checks.method: Google Analytics 4 and Meta Pixel must each have sent at least one network request during the session.
checks.detail: Both required tags fired. Google Analytics 4: 15 requests; Meta Pixel: 15 requests.

checks.label: Nothing fires twice
checks.question: Is the page counting the same thing more than once?
checks.method: A SHA-1 fingerprint of vendor + event name + payload, with every param that changes on every hit removed first. Two requests sharing a fingerprint are the same beacon sent twice, not two legitimate events.

checks.label: The data actually arrives
checks.question: Does the data reach the platforms, or does it die on the way?
checks.method: Any tracking request answered with a 4xx or 5xx, plus any request that failed at the transport layer and never got a response at all. Grouped by vendor and status.
checks.detail: 1 of 163 tracking requests failed to arrive.

checks.label: One account per platform
checks.question: Is the data all landing in the same account, or split across several?
checks.method: For each vendor, count the distinct account / property / pixel IDs seen. More than one means the traffic is being split.

checks.label: Add to cart gets tracked
checks.question: When someone adds to cart, do the ad platforms find out?
checks.method: During the add-to-cart phase specifically, each installed ad platform must have received at least one event matching a commercial-intent pattern. If no add-to-cart button could be found, this is recorded as not applicable rather than pass or fail.
checks.detail: Snap Pixel, Criteo received no conversion event after the click.

checks.label: Event names make sense to the platforms
checks.question: Will the ad platforms understand the events they are being sent?
checks.method: Each Meta and GA4 event name is checked for membership in that platform's published standard event vocabulary. Names outside it are custom and cannot drive built-in optimisation.

checks.label: Nothing dead is still running
checks.question: Is the page still sending data to a system that was switched off?
checks.method: Any hit to the Universal Analytics /collect endpoint. Universal Analytics stopped processing data in July 2024; these requests go nowhere.
checks.detail: No traffic to deprecated Universal Analytics endpoints.
